node.title: Random-prime typicality model for zone-(b) collisions (grounded by E1)
node.statement: The official-scale prime behaves collision-typically: #collisions at quotient order N' matches the random-prime expectation #pairs * E[Omega(Norm)] / pi(range) — negligible at the open cells (N' >= 128, log2 A >= 100, log2 p ~ 250), and with collision ONSET at the birthday scale of a 2^49.7 support for the feasible N'=64 cell (~2^25 samples). Via collision_norm_criterion + thm:upstairs this is exactly 'p divides none of the bounded-height difference norms beyond chance'.
node.attack_surface: the N'=64 decisive run tests the model QUANTITATIVELY (onset curve, not just presence); the R4 conspiracy search attacks it adversarially (hunt primes dividing many norms); are_exceptional_density proves it for almost all primes
node.falsifier: CORRECTED: the N'=64 cell tests NOTHING (fullness there is unconditionally forced by graded_collision_radius — E1's zero collisions were a theorem, not evidence). The model's support is the density theorem + the R4 conspiracy search; no sampling test reaches its open content at N' >= 128.
node.notes: the E1 pilot's zero-collision data is consistent with the model; the model converts the un-sampleable open cells into a per-prime typicality question with a provable almost-all backstop (Pilot packet ref: PR #180's e1_row_c_value_set_sampling.md — repoint on integration.)
